slot.brief: A hot body cools in a room; given cooling data over one interval, ask for its temperature after another equal interval using Newton's law of cooling.

stem: A body cools from 80 °C to 50 °C in 4 minutes in a room maintained at 20 °C. Assuming Newton's law of cooling, its temperature after another 4 minutes will be:

verdicts.working: By Newton’s law, excess temperature decays exponentially. It falls from 80−20=60°C to 50−20=30°C in 4 minutes, so in the next 4 minutes it halves again to 15°C. Thus the body reaches 20+15=35°C.

working:
First interval: (80 - 50)/4 = k((80 + 50)/2 - 20) => 7.5 = k*45, k = 1/6 per min. Second interval: (50 - T)/4 = (1/6)((50 + T)/2 - 20). Solving gives T = 35 °C.

Independent check: By Newton’s law, excess temperature decays exponentially. It falls from 80−20=60°C to 50−20=30°C in 4 minutes, so in the next 4 minutes it halves again to 15°C. Thus the body reaches 20+15=35°C.
solution:
By Newton’s law of cooling, the excess temperature above the room temperature decays exponentially. In 4 minutes it falls from $80-20=60^\circ\mathrm C$ to $50-20=30^\circ\mathrm C$, i.e. it halves; after another 4 minutes it halves again to $15^\circ\mathrm C$.
$$T=20+15=35^\circ\mathrm C$$
